column1: # The DUPLICATION DOCKET — one row per tag that two or more production files claim.
# Written by hand; `python3 tools/citations.py dups` reads it, and `dups --check`
# (in `make fast`) fails on a row that has none.
# ⚠ A ROW HERE IS A QUESTION THAT HAS BEEN ANSWERED, NOT A DEFECT.  Two files citing
# one rule may be one algorithm written twice — or one CONSTRAINT binding both, or two
# halves of a split the rule itself describes.  The verdict says which, with the
# argument, so nobody re-derives it next session.
# ⚠ AND THE FILE COUNT IS PART OF THE VERDICT.  A verdict is about the sites that were
# READ; when a new file claims the rule, the count no longer matches and the row goes
# back on the docket.  That is what makes "this becomes a duplicate at three" a
# mechanism rather than a hope.
#   one         a genuine duplicate implementation — an open debt, merge it
#   merged      it was `one`; the merge has landed
#   broad       the RULE is too broad — the two sites are different things, sharpen it upstream
#   constraint  the tag names a rule that BINDS many sites, not an algorithm implemented once
#   inherent    really two, and the difference belongs to the application
# tag
@HB-X69
column4: Thickness is palette-side, so a cell stores an id. That binds the palette reader, the selection, the wire, the plan's stroke, the octagon body and the field — six sites obeying one constraint, none of them an algorithm.

column1: @HB-X70
column4: An opening is never absence. It binds the gesture that makes one, the session that picks its material, the mesher that draws it and the wire message — four obligations, one rule.

column1: @HB-X31
column4: No odd multiple of 15 degrees exists. One library site obeys it; probe/h1 MEASURES it, which is the validation the rule asks for, not a second implementation.

column1: X2
column4: `WS_CONCURRENT` is declared once in hex_voxel; editor_server is its one consumer, discussing the case it names.
The authoring residual bound. session obeys it, probe/m1p measures it.
One upstream fact — the in-between period is 6.245 wu — justifying two independent choices: the reach's UNIT in session, and why the aim refusal is reachable in hex_editor. Neither computes it.
The agreement law binds `aim` and `run` and forbids mixing them in one gesture; probe/m2p measures the agreement. Four obligations plus its measurement.

column1: @HB-X24
column4: There is no square sublattice of a hexagonal lattice, so a lattice polygon cannot be a rectangle. hex_editor cites it where the footprint must not assume one; probe/pc cites it as the measured EXPLANATION for `house_recover` refusing all 18 promoted floors. A fact that binds, and its measurement.

column1: @HB-X12
column4: The rule describes a SPLIT — the cell carries an id, the palette carries the float — so both halves cite it. `moros_map/src/palette.loft` says so in its own words: "`@HB-X12` is the rule; this file is the other half of it."

column1: @HB-X49
column4: Two DRIVERS of one gesture, verified rather than assumed: `editor_run` and `editor_server` both reach `press_verb` -> `tower_ring`, and `hex_shape::arc_fill` is called only in gesture.loft. The prose is near-identical; the code is one body.

column1: @HB-X29
column4: A FACT that binds: no library derives the 1.1021 degree bias, they cite it — session for the gate's walk, gesture twice (the D conversion, and promote-on-close's reason that linework need not meet a corner), hex_editor at the call site. probe/h1 measures whether the bias is UNIFORM and probe/m1p what authoring RESOLUTION follows; those are its validation, not a second implementation.

column1: @HB-X45
column4: One rule — a convex form's description is recovered from its CELLS, exactly and constructively — cited at the primitive that acts on it (`promote_close`, which is why a closed loop must gain a floor) and at its call site in `press_verb`. A rule stated where it binds, twice, not derived either time.

column1: @HB-X68
column4: ⚠ WATCHED. One doorstep contract (ordinal offers, nominal refuses without one) carried by two structs — `hex_editor::Fit` and `hex_part::SocketFit` — which differ because each package answers in its own shape (a sentence plus ok, versus a code). A shared type needs a package below both, and the name `Fit` has already collided across this graph. A THIRD carrier makes this `one`.
